- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive (especially >0.5) and recent history shows upward momentum.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially <0.0) or neutral, especially after recent spikes.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes in sentiment; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% for 3–5 day horizon.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–3% per day until convergence.
- Lagged sentiment: if sentiment peaks 2–3 days prior, model should adjust forecast downward by 1–2% to account for delayed reaction.
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; cap forecast range within ±3% of 14-day moving average.
